study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Zabihi et al., Biological Psychiatry: Cognitive Neuroscience and Neuroimaging, 2019
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Dissecting the Heterogeneous Cortical Anatomy of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Normative Models

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Gaussian process regression (GPR) was used to estimate separate normative models of cortical thickness and surface area at each vertex on the cortical surface. The model used a covariance function combining linear and non-linear terms with automatic relevance determination parameters. The model was trained on TD cohort (n=206) and validated using 10-fold cross-validation.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Gaussian process regression (43) was used to estimate separate normative models of CT and SA at each vertex on the cortical surface.; we generated a developmental model of typical brain development by training a Gaussian process regression model on the TD cohort (n = 206) using age and gender as covariates
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Zabihi2019.pdf.md: Methods and Materials / Constructing a Normative Model of CT (lines 68-72); 1-s2.0-S245190221830329X-mmc1.pdf.md: Supplementary methods / Gaussian process regression (lines 15-27)

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Cortical thickness (CT) was the primary response variable, with surface area (SA) analyzed as a secondary measure. Both measures were estimated at each vertex on the cortical surface using FreeSurfer version 5.3. Cortical thickness maps were smoothed with a 10-mm surface-based Gaussian kernel.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: here we focused on CT, which is a sensitive and reliable measure of cortical morphology in ASD (6,8,39), although we also investigated SA.; FreeSurfer (version 5.3; https://surfer.nmr.mgh.harvard.edu/) was used to estimate measures of regional CT and SA.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Zabihi2019.pdf.md: Introduction (line 27) and Methods and Materials / Participants (line 66); 1-s2.0-S245190221830329X-mmc1.pdf.md: Supplementary methods / Magnetic Resonance Imaging (lines 11-14)

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age and gender (sex) were used as covariates in the primary normative model. In supplementary analyses, additional covariates including IQ, scanning site, and FreeSurfer Euler number were included to check for potential confounds.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: we generated a developmental model of typical brain development by training a Gaussian process regression model on the TD cohort (n = 206) using age and gender as covariates (i.e., independent variables) to predict CT (i.e., dependent variable).; we estimated a separate normative model additionally including dummy regressors for IQ, site, and FreeSurfer Euler number
